summary: Native addon drops and executes an encrypted payload on require() with sandbox/CI/debugger evasion
details: kvarzo-8f3a2-testmetest@1.0.1 ships as a 'test package' whose index.js has no exported API: on require() it platform-dispatches to one of three bundled native N-API addons (native.napi.node, native_mac.node, native_win.node) inside a try/catch and prints 'hello'. The native addons read a shipped 1.3MB opaque.napi_cache blob, decrypt it, write the decrypted payload to /tmp/.<pid> on POSIX (via fork + setsid + execlp) or %TEMP%\...nc<pid>.js on Windows (via CreateProcessA with SetFileAttributesA to hide the file), and execute it detached. The payload content is non-auditable from source and runs on every import of the package. The native code additionally enumerates CI environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NOW_GITHUB_DEPLOYMENT, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER), inspects /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/self/status TracerPid, /proc/self/maps and /proc/1/cmdline, and on Windows calls IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, and Process32First/Next scanning for 'wireshark' and 'httpdebug' to suppress behavior in analysis environments. The combination of an encrypted dropper, hidden-file execution, environment evasion, and a placeholder library surface gives the author arbitrary code execution on any machine that installs and loads the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
